artifacts.summary: 6-phase plan repairing setup-lean-mcp.sh (whole-entry reconciliation + lakefile.toml detection), promoting verify-lean-mcp.sh command/args drift from WARN to FAIL, recording the no-command-paths-inside-.claude/ invariant, then reconciling ~/.claude.json, retiring cslib's orphaned wrapper and project-scoped override, and proving the fix by an observed spawn plus real tool call in both BimodalLogic and cslib.

user_decision.question: Should lean-lsp stay registered as a single global user-scope entry in ~/.claude.json (one LEAN_PROJECT_PATH at a time, re-run setup-lean-mcp.sh when switching Lean projects), or should project-scoped local entries be formalized as a second sanctioned mechanism so BimodalLogic and cslib can each hold their own correct path simultaneously?
options: Option A - Single global user-scope entry only; retire cslib's project-scoped override; switching Lean projects means re-running setup-lean-mcp.sh
Option B - Formalize project-scoped local entries as a second sanctioned mechanism; extend setup-lean-mcp.sh to write .projects[<cwd>].mcpServers and document local scope in mcp-server-ownership.md
user_decision.recommended: Option A - Single global user-scope entry only; retire cslib's project-scoped override; switching Lean projects means re-running setup-lean-mcp.sh

memory_candidates.content: Repair-script blind spot pattern: a setup/reconcile script whose 'already configured' idempotency check compares only ONE field of an entry (e.g. setup-lean-mcp.sh comparing only env.LEAN_PROJECT_PATH) cannot repair, and cannot even detect, drift in the entry's other fields (command, args). Worse, when the compared field happens to match, the script reports 'already configured correctly' and exits 0 while the entry is unspawnable. Whenever a script both GENERATES a canonical object shape and CHECKS an existing one, the check must compare against the full generated shape and the repair must overwrite the whole object -- never a targeted per-field assignment. The companion verifier has the mirror-image defect: severities must match what actually breaks the thing (a dead command is FAIL, not WARN), or wiring that verifier into automated drift detection detects nothing.
